cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jonathan, Saul's son, hears the order and delights greatly in David anyway. He doesn't go along with it. He goes and warns David (1 Samuel 19:2). Picture your boss handing you a job, and you walking straight to the person it's about, friends, just to say, "Heads up."

The answer is to find a secret place and hide. Jonathan tells David, “find a secret place and hide there.” (1 Samuel 19:2). Short and clear. Jonathan adds that he will stand beside his father in the field and ask about David (1 Samuel 19:3).

The answer is that David struck down the Philistine. Jonathan says, “He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel.” (1 Samuel 19:5). He's pointing at something Saul watched with his own eyes. That's a strong way to argue with a king, friends.

The answer is that Saul rejoiced. Jonathan tells his father, “You saw it and rejoiced…” (1 Samuel 19:5). Think about how that lands, friends. Jonathan is basically saying, "Dad, you were there, and you were glad."

The answer is innocent. Jonathan asks, “…why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?” (1 Samuel 19:5). Two phrases, one point: David hasn't done anything to deserve this. Jonathan says it right to his father's face.

The answer is that Saul swears an oath to spare David. Saul swears, “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.” (1 Samuel 19:6). That's a big promise from the same man who just gave the opposite order. Jonathan's words got through, friends.

The answer is True. Jonathan summons David, tells him all these things, and brings him to Saul, and “…David was with Saul as before.” (1 Samuel 19:7). Jonathan is the one who brings him back. I bet that felt a little tense, friends.

The word is fled. David struck the Philistines “…with such a mighty blow that they fled before him.” (1 Samuel 19:8). Imagine opening the door to a game, friends, and the other team is already sprinting for the parking lot.

The answer is that Saul tries to pin David to the wall, and this part is heavy. Saul “…tried to pin him to the wall with his spear.” (1 Samuel 19:10). David is just playing the harp when it happens. The text says a spirit of distress from the LORD had come upon Saul (1 Samuel 19:9).

The answer is False. The spear doesn't hit David. The text says, “…David eluded him and the spear struck the wall.” (1 Samuel 19:10). That wall got quite a surprise, friends. David fled and escaped that night.

The answer is the window. “…Michal lowered David from the window, and he ran away and escaped.” (1 Samuel 19:12). Michal is David's wife. Saul's messengers are watching the house, so the window is the exit. She had warned him first: “If you do not run for your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead!” (1 Samuel 19:11).

The answer is hair. Michal takes a household idol, lays it in the bed, and puts “…some goat hair on its head, and covered it with a garment.” (1 Samuel 19:13). That's a stand-in sleeper built from whatever she had on hand, friends. From the doorway, a quick look might just work.

The answer is "He is ill." When Saul sends the messengers to seize David, Michal says, “He is ill.” (1 Samuel 19:14). Just two words, and the whole plan rides on them. David is already gone, so the bed has to do the talking.

The answer is to bring David up in his bed, and this one is heavy. Saul tells the messengers, “Bring him up to me in his bed so I can kill him.” (1 Samuel 19:15). Being told David is ill doesn't slow Saul down. He sends the messengers right back.

The answer is that David threatened to kill her. Michal tells Saul, “He said to me, ‘Help me get away, or I will kill you!’…” (1 Samuel 19:17). It's her answer to the king's question. The messengers found the idol, and now she has to explain, friends.

The answer is True. David goes to Samuel, the prophet, at Ramah and tells him “…all that Saul had done to him.” (1 Samuel 19:18). All of it. I bet that took a while to tell, friends. Then he and Samuel go to Naioth and stay there (1 Samuel 19:18).

The answer is that they begin to prophesy. The messengers see the group of prophets with Samuel leading them. Then “…the Spirit of God came upon them, and Saul’s messengers also began to prophesy.” (1 Samuel 19:20). Their to-do list just changed completely, friends.

The answer is False. Saul “…sent messengers a third time, and even they began to prophesy.” (1 Samuel 19:21). Three tries, and David was never delivered. That's a tough run for Saul's messenger service, friends.

The answer is that he walks along prophesying. The Spirit of God comes upon even Saul, “…and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.” (1 Samuel 19:23). Back at the cistern at Secu, he had asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” (1 Samuel 19:22). Now he's walking along prophesying.

The answer is that he collapses and lies there all day and night. Saul strips off his robes and prophesies before Samuel, “And he collapsed and lay naked all that day and night.” (1 Samuel 19:24). The writer tells it plainly. Saul came to catch David and spent a whole day and night on the ground instead, friends.

The answer is prophets. The saying is, “Is Saul also among the prophets?” (1 Samuel 19:24). It comes after he prophesies before Samuel. Once a saying like that gets started, friends, it follows you around like cookie crumbs on an apron.
